text.p: Bonds opened firmer in line with the European trend, with the spread between the Portuguese and the Spanish 10-years remaining steady at five basis points, traders said.

Further gains at the longer end will continue to depend on the evolution of other markets, they added, but the shorter end could see more activity linked to expectations for a good inflation figure for June.
They said that some traders were beginning to bet that a low inflation number would be followed by a Bank of Portugal rate cut.
"The 10-years have already reached the spread target of 70 basis points (with the Bund) so there is little room for autonomous gains," said one trader.
The futures contract faced strong resistance around 111.25 which would be difficult to break today, said one futures trader.
